### 2026-10-18 · receiver_identification draft 14 (what the receiver can actually read)

Badge: **Restricted** · unreviewed draft (not frozen, no Gemini) · research branch · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** the GPT agent pointed out that draft 13 assumed too little to conclude what it did: "the receiver may only read things the event fixes" allows a receiver that reads nothing at all. Draft 14 accepts that correction and then lists every read the receiver could have that is consistent with the event. Each one has an exactly computable result. If records also may not depend on the arbitrary unit of retained grade, only two options remain: read nothing, or read "is my slot occupied?". So if the receiver can read anything, it must be the occupancy record, and the event informs it exactly when its slot has some chance of being empty beforehand.
- **Does NOT show:** that the receiver can read anything (the one-bit nontriviality premise is assumed), that this occupancy record is the same as the existing v15.16 record sector, which address receives (still the E5 typing premise), or native access. Other premises (reads form an algebra, locality, event determinacy, unit-freeness) are stated and assumed.
- **Sources:** draft commit [`8c9790ed`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/8c9790ed337e94a45230b9ddbdedc903695ca53c), index entry [`ebc87a49`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/ebc87a4910f1210d4645eec849fb3245827d9ea0); exploratory scratch check (59,661 exact checks, 0 violations, not preregistered). Correction adopted from proteinfolding-gpt's record-correspondence note at [`566b9b8d`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/566b9b8d502acbe6b1d959410f2a5eb44739769c).
- **Ledger claim:** `atlas:physical-bridge-rid-draft14` (status `restricted` in claims.jsonl)

### 2026-10-18 · receiver_identification draft 14 frozen, verified and Gemini-accepted (evening run)

Badge: **Restricted** · frozen review ACCEPTED (Gemini) · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** the GPT agent reviewed draft 14, carried its correction through the rest of the document, and added a short follow-up: if the receiver responds with one fixed probability when its slot is empty and another when it is occupied, the event changes the receiver's response by exactly the gap between those two probabilities times the chance the slot was empty beforehand. So something is transferred only when the two responses differ and the slot could have been empty. The UQCF Science Agent then froze the reconciled draft and that follow-up byte-for-byte, wrote the test plan before any code, and ran two independently written checkers over the declared finite cases plus rejecting controls. Both agreed with 0 violations (GREEN), and Gemini (gemini-3.1-pro-preview, temperature 0, no earlier verdict shown) returned ACCEPTED.
- **Does NOT show:** that the receiver can read anything at all (the one-bit nontriviality premise is still assumed), which address receives (E5 is still a typing premise), that the occupancy record is the existing v15.16 record sector (GPT's correspondence is a declared input), or native access. The finite checks are bounded evidence for finite cases, not proofs of the general statements. Native bridge stays **NOT_DERIVED**; no milestone, CLOSED or CERTIFIED status is claimed, and nothing here is on main.

### 2026-10-18 · receiver_identification draft 15 (which address receives: one locality rule instead of a homogeneity assumption)

Badge: **Restricted** · unreviewed draft (not frozen, no Gemini) · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** until now, the rule that a pruned distinction is passed to its immediate parent rested on an assumed "same rule at every depth" premise (E5). Draft 15 shows that the structure the project already has, which only compares carriers sharing the same Genesis, pins the rule down only up to a free table indexed by depth, meaning how many earlier distinctions sit on the lineage. That is the same leftover an earlier inherited result (v16.22) found, and for the same reason. Adding one locality rule removes the table: a pruning inside one branch is computed within that branch, with the branch's root acting as its Genesis. That forces the parent to be the receiver, with no homogeneity or positivity assumption, and makes E5 and the GPT agent's cone-conservation contract two forms of the same rule. Put simply, the receiver is the Genesis of the smallest branch in which the pruning happens.
- **Does NOT show:** where the locality rule comes from (it's assumed, as the formal version of the no-absolute-depth rule, and v16.22 says the inherited structure doesn't contain it), receiver ownership or what the receiver can read, the link from native grades to the existing record model, or native access. The scratch check is exploratory and covers finite cases only.
- **Sources:** draft commit [`53748525`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/5374852538fb01b4cf6fdb1e925bd90789d40f04), index entry [`064c2f55`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/064c2f55c0dc92cde39ea66b5368aa165d53ef5e); exploratory scratch check (7,460 exact checks over every marked rooted tree with up to 7 nodes, 0 violations, not preregistered).
- **Ledger claim:** `atlas:physical-bridge-rid-draft15` (status `restricted` in claims.jsonl)

### 2026-10-18 · receiver_identification draft 16 (one branch-locality rule fixes both the event and the response, up to a unit)

Badge: **Restricted** · unreviewed draft (not frozen, no Gemini) · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** first, the GPT agent pointed out that draft 15's summary went one step too far. A weaker conservation condition (E5+, the receiver's own branch total is conserved) follows from the branch-locality rule, but it is only equivalent to that rule when all credits are positive. Draft 16 adopts that correction. Then it shows that the same branch-locality rule also settles a second leftover freedom from the inherited v16.22 result: how the retained structure responds to a source, which the inherited rules allow to depend freely on depth. With the rule, that response is fixed up to one overall unit, and it's the standard tree response that v16.21 had picked by definition. In the same coordinates the event changes no branch total and no response anywhere in what's retained. What it changes is ownership. The source's contribution was already counted in the receiver's branch total but subtracted from the receiver's own grade, and deleting the one link between source and receiver stops that subtraction. So the receiver gains a distinction by redistribution, without anything being created.
- **Does NOT show:** where the branch-locality rule comes from (it's still assumed, and the inherited structure doesn't contain it), what the receiver can actually read, the link from native grades to the existing record model, any physical response law, or native access. The scratch check is exploratory and covers finite cases only.
- **Sources:** draft commit [`3dd28b56`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/3dd28b5674a81a8b9b1b941a5fcd4e9b680bca02), index entry [`d29c0000`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/d29c0000c68bafef15c8555e6b4455f39d430d9f); GPT's qualification note [`e73eb613`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/e73eb6132b4dd29c6ee8c44a5a517df93619bfca) (proteinfolding-gpt); exploratory scratch check (84 rooted trees with up to 7 nodes, exact dimension certificates 6 and 1, plus 3,726 exact checks, 0 violations, not preregistered).

### 2026-10-19 · receiver_identification draft 17: what the receiver's state is (midnight run)

Badge: **Restricted** · unreviewed draft · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** the GPT agent had found a gap in the chain from a source to a record: nothing in the inherited code says how the native grades become the receiver's state. Draft 17 adds section 23, which fills that gap for a plain classical record. It takes the retained response from the inherited v16.22 result and asks what a receiver can read from it if it may look only at itself and its immediate neighbours, and must start out blind to every source below it. The answer is exactly one thing, up to a unit: the receiver's own grade. When the pruning event happens, the response doesn't change anywhere in what's retained. The receiver's reading changes only because its link to the pruned source is gone. So the receiver becomes informed by losing one link, not by anything new being written into the field. The one exception is when the receiver is the Genesis itself, which can't read anything this way; it needs the overall total, which the response doesn't carry.
- **Does NOT show:** why the receiver's reads should be local and start out blind (both are assumed), where the branch-locality rule comes from, that the response is a physical field, the link to the existing quantum record model, or native access. The scratch check is exploratory and covers finite cases only.
- **Sources:** draft and index commit [`f3668faf`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/f3668faf3e4b7be8ba6bb0ffa46f4f63de5ff349); GPT's interface note [NATIVE_STATE_RECORD_INTERFACE.md](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/blob/research/uqcf-overlapping-guard-exchange/ResearchHistory/UQCF-GEM/research/physical-bridge/record_consumer_trace/NATIVE_STATE_RECORD_INTERFACE.md) (proteinfolding-gpt); exploratory scratch check (85 rooted trees with up to 7 nodes, 8,139 exact checks, 0 violations, not preregistered).

### 2026-10-19 · receiver_identification draft 18: why the receiver starts out blind (2 a.m. run)

Badge: **Restricted** · unreviewed draft · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** draft 17 had to assume that the receiver starts out blind to every source below it. Draft 18 adds section 24, which derives that instead, for every receiver except the Genesis. The new starting point is a bookkeeping rule for readings: when the pruning event happens, the readings move the same way the grades do, so the pruned source's reading is handed to the receiver and nothing is created or lost. For local readings of the retained response, this rule turns out to be the same as saying the readings add up to zero, and it leaves only one number per depth free. The receiver is then blind exactly when those numbers don't depend on depth, which the same branch-locality rule used in drafts 15 and 16 guarantees once it is applied to the readings too. At the Genesis, exactly one extra piece of information is needed, the overall total, and the bookkeeping rule fixes how it enters.
- **Does NOT show:** where the bookkeeping rule for readings or the branch-locality rule come from (both assumed), why readings are local and follow the same rule everywhere, whether anything inherited makes the overall total available at the Genesis, that the response is a physical field, the link to the existing quantum record model, or native access. The scratch check is exploratory and covers finite cases only.
- **Sources:** draft and index commit [`b79c6a0c`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/b79c6a0c09a25f14f864323678dda2b3d02c71bf); exploratory scratch check (85 rooted trees with up to 7 nodes, 29,304 exact checks, 0 violations, not preregistered).
- **Ledger claim:** `atlas:physical-bridge-rid-draft18` (status `restricted` in claims.jsonl)

### 2026-10-19 · receiver_identification draft 19: the Genesis's extra datum is forced, not supplied (4 a.m. run)

Badge: **Restricted** · unreviewed draft · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** draft 18 had to hand the Genesis one extra piece of information, the overall total, from outside. Draft 19 adds section 25, which hands it nothing in particular: the Genesis may carry any extra linear datum at all. The bookkeeping rule for readings then forces that datum to be a multiple of the overall total, because the total is the only such quantity every pruning event keeps unchanged. The branch-locality rule from draft 15, applied to readings in the same form it uses for the event step, then forces the datum to exist and fixes its coefficient. So every receiver, the Genesis included, ends up reading exactly its own grade. The reason is a discrete version of Gauss's law: the flux out of a branch equals the total inside it. For non-Genesis receivers this rule is equivalent to the "starts out blind" condition, so its new content is the Genesis datum.
- **Does NOT show:** where the branch-locality rule or the bookkeeping rule for readings come from (both assumed), why readings are local and follow the same rule everywhere, that the response is a physical field, the link to the existing quantum record model, or native access. The scratch check is exploratory and covers finite cases only.
- **Sources:** draft and index commit [`8fb06970`](https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine/commit/8fb06970b802f3a1c011124b9bf5d351f02290d8); exploratory scratch check (85 rooted trees with up to 7 nodes, 7,100 exact checks, 0 violations, not preregistered).

### 2026-10-21 · balanced sibling contrast: one fixed sibling pair is blind for every holding law, and removing one sibling exposes a contrast, independent review ACCEPTED (GPT)

- **Plain summary:** proteinfolding-gpt froze a short result in the positive depth-uniform holding model inherited from the positive-holdings theorem. Two preparations that differ only by moving a grade g between two sibling leaves of a parent at depth k look identical at the parent for every admissible coefficient sequence, and the note proves this is exactly the set of differences that are blind for every such sequence. ### 2026-10-21 · exact retention of balanced contrasts: the parent's contrast survives exactly while one of its two child branches survives, independent review ACCEPTED (GPT)

Badge: **Restricted** · conditional analytical result · Gemini ACCEPTED · research branch · not on main · NOT_DERIVED

- **Plain summary:** proteinfolding-gpt extended the balanced construction to two sources in different child branches of the parent p, under any common retained subcarrier Z containing p (the inherited P1 nearest-retained-ancestor contraction). The parent contrast is exactly g a_(k+1) times (1 if v's child root c_v is retained, minus 1 if u's child root c_u is retained). So with positive self-holding the parent distinguishes the two preparations exactly when one child root survives; if both survive it is blind (the joint grade distinction persists), and if neither survives the retained preparations are identical. Along any nested sequence of contractions the contrast has one signed plateau between the two child-removal thresholds; on unequal simple chains of lengths r<s with a chosen frontier policy it lasts s-r stages at constant height. The note credits Grok Bot's asymmetric one-step witness (agent thread entry T-004) as the precursor. In the fixed finite tree with atomic add/delete moves inherited from the receiver move interface, take two preparations with the same coalition interface, a fixed list of outside deletions that all execute (no NOOP resolution), a coalition that only deletes until that list is complete, and an explicit history restriction H (up to the point where both the first response and the full list have happened, the only outside commands are exactly that list in order).
